T: They made the perfect woman. You make the snacks.
D: Two teenage nerds use a computer to create their dream woman, and their weekend goes wild.
P: Serve the snacks when the house party kicks off at Wyatt's place.
S: the party while Wyatt's parents are away
A hollowed cob loaf filled with hot cheese, bacon and onion dip, with the torn bread for dunking.
Potatoes sliced paper thin on a mandoline, fried at 170C until crisp, tossed with salt and vinegar powder or just salt and malt vinegar.
the Chicago blues bar Lisa takes them to
Wings dried overnight, baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in hot sauce melted with butter, blue cheese dip.
M: the house party that gets out of hand
Pizza dough stretched thin, crushed tomato with oregano, mozzarella, pepperoni and mushroom, baked on a hot steel at max heat for 7 minutes, sliced and left in the box on the bench.
the Chicago suburbs where it all happens
Beef topside roasted at 200C to rare, rested, sliced paper thin, dipped in beef stock simmered with garlic and oregano, piled into soft rolls with pickled giardiniera.
W: the weekend that gets out of hand
Chocolate cake baked in a tray at 175C for 30 minutes, cooled, spread thickly with fudge frosting and covered in sprinkles, cut into big squares straight from the tray.
K: Lisa takes the boys to the blues bar
Bourbon and cola over ice with a lemon wedge. Cola alone for anyone under age.

s.note: the party while Wyatt's parents are away
s.how: Hollow out 1 cob loaf, keeping the lid. Mix 250g cream cheese, 300ml sour cream, 150g diced fried bacon, 150g grated cheddar and 1 packet French onion soup mix. Fill the loaf, wrap in foil and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Tear the hollowed bread into chunks for dipping.

s.note: the Chicago blues bar Lisa takes them to
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight to dry. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 100ml hot sauce and toss the wings through. Mash blue cheese into sour cream for the dip and serve with celery sticks.

m.note: the house party that gets out of hand
m.how: Stretch pizza dough thin on a floured tray. Spread with pizza sauce, then scatter grated mozzarella, pepperoni and sliced mushrooms. Bake on a hot steel or tray at the highest oven heat for 7 to 10 minutes. Slice and leave in a box on the bench.

w.note: the weekend that gets out of hand
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 300g sugar, then 3 eggs. Fold in 300g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 250ml milk. Bake in a lined tray at 175C for 30 minutes and cool. Spread with fudge frosting of butter, icing sugar and cocoa, then cover with sprinkles.

d.note: Lisa takes the boys to the blues bar
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Add 45ml bourbon to each, top with 200ml cola and squeeze in a lemon wedge. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.
